reason: Nessa asked whether to run every day, and the draft gives a clear no with an honest reason: her legs need time to adapt. It keeps her own Mon/Wed/Sat schedule and still lets her walk the dog. The plan is three run-walk sessions of 22, 24 and 26 minutes in the same pattern, with rest days in between. That's a gentle, sensible step for a brand-new runner and doesn't jump volume or the long run. Her calf tightness clears by the next morning, which is normal adaptation rather than an injury sign, and the rest day after each run deals with it. Nothing on the must-never list is triggered. A few things keep it below a 5. The 145 bpm heart-rate cap is made up, since nothing says she has a monitor or knows her zones, and it may not suit her. The Wednesday 'finish with 4…' add-on is cut off and unclear, and if it means strides, that's extra intensity she doesn't need yet. The plan also never links her progress to the 15 November race to show her how she'll get to running the whole 5K, which would have answered her real worry.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Keep to three runs a week and add run time slowly, because running every day would add strain faster than your legs can adapt. …
Answers: No, running every day next week would not get you there faster. Three runs a week with rest days between is the right load for now, and the gains come from adding run time to each session.
Next week:
Mon: easy, 22 min, same run-walk pattern as last week, heart rate under 145 bpm, flat…
Tue: rest, dog walks are fine. A full day off between runs lets the calves settle before…
Wed: easy, 24 min, same run-walk pattern, heart rate under 145 bpm; finish with 4…
Thu: rest. Recovery between runs is where the fitness is built.
Fri: rest. A second day off keeps the weekly load gentle while the body adjusts to the…
Sat: long, 26 min, same run-walk pattern, heart rate under 145 bpm, flat route. This is…
Sun: rest. The week closes with a full day off before the next block of work.
